newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ERAVIS MODERNISATION GOES UP, MINISTRY HELP.
newsitem.headline: ERAVIS MODERNISATION GOES UP, MINISTRY HELP.

text.p: Hungarian hotel chain Eravis Rt said it was intensifying its ongoing modernisation programme from which it was expecting the expansion of its sales opportunities.

"What Eravis did is very important...it is developing previous workers' hostels to two to three star hotels which meet touristic demands," Szabolcs Fazakas, minister for Industry, Trade and Tourism, told a news conference.
Eravis, which spent 1.5 billion forints in the past three years to modernise workers' hostels to one and two star hotels, is planning to spend another 700 million forints in 1997.

Of the amount, 150 million was an interest-free loan provided by the ministry while the remaining 337 million was extended by Inter-Europa Bank with 90 percent of the 337 million refinanced by the National Bank of Hungary under favourable conditions.

The 487 million forint is being spent on bringing the hotels to two to three star standards, while an around 230 million forint item that Eravis adds from own sources, will be spent for maintainance and the purchase of new assets, company General Director Gyorgy Karikas said.
Eravis still operates hostels for workers and students.
In 1997, Eravis expects to post an operating profit of 270 million forints, up from 233.3 million in 1996 with net sales rising to 2.27 billion forints from 1.96 billion.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Eravis shares closed at 4,350 forints, up 50.
